stem:
Yamini's school has two taps on the same tank. Tap A alone fills the tank in $5$ days. Tap B alone fills the tank in $20$ days. Both taps run together on that tank.

Which claim correctly finds how long they take together?

options.text: The answer is the one-day rate itself, reported as the filling time.
Add the filling times to get $5+20=25$ days.
The one-day rates are $\dfrac{1}{5}$ and $\dfrac{1}{20}$; together $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the tank fills per day, so the tank fills in $4$ days.
Adding the one-day rates also gives the fill time when Tap A runs alone for some days and then Tap B runs alone afterwards.

teacher.key_rationale: Combined rate $\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{1}{4}$ tank per day, so time is $4$ days. Reporting the rate as time, adding the day-counts, or stretching to sequential work miss that hinge.
